COMMON.ENABLED_HINT: Turn on once the configuration below is complete.
COMMON.SECRET_KEEP_HINT: Saved value is hidden — leave empty to keep the current one.

WHATSAPP.NOTIF_INTRO: Send order and invoice notifications over WhatsApp via the Meta Cloud API.
WHATSAPP.INFOBIP_INTRO: Configure your Infobip WhatsApp credentials. Both Base URL and API key are required.
WHATSAPP.WASENDER_INTRO: When enabled, WhatsApp messages are routed through WaSender. This provider does not require template approval — messages are delivered directly.
WHATSAPP.WASENDER_BASEURL_HINT: Optional. Defaults to https://wasenderapi.com when left blank.
WHATSAPP.ERR_INFOBIP_URL: Enter a valid Infobip base URL (…​.infobip.com).
WHATSAPP.ERR_SENDER: Enter a valid sender (phone in E.164, e.g. +9737…).

SMS.INFOBIP_INTRO: When enabled, SMS is routed through Infobip. Otherwise SMS falls back to the default system provider.
SMS.BAREED_INTRO: When enabled, SMS is routed through BareedSMS. Otherwise SMS falls back to the default system provider.
SMS.SENDER_HINT: Alphanumeric sender ID (e.g. InfoSMS, max 11 chars) or a phone number. What's allowed depends on your account and the destination country.
SMS.BAREED_SENDER_HINT: Optional. Alphanumeric sender ID (max 11 chars) or a phone number. If left empty, the account default is used.
SMS.ERR_SENDER: Enter a valid alphanumeric ID (3–11 chars) or phone number.

SMTP.TITLE: Email SMTP
SMTP.INTRO: When enabled, outbound email is sent through this SMTP server. Use port 465 with SSL on, or port 587 with SSL off (STARTTLS).
SMTP.PASSWORD_HINT: For Gmail, Yahoo and most providers this must be an app password, not your account password.
SMTP.FROM_HINT: Address that appears in the recipient's inbox. Usually matches the SMTP username.

TEMPLATES.TITLE: WhatsApp templates
TEMPLATES.DISABLED_WARNING: Enable and save the plugin to sync templates.
TEMPLATES.CONFIRM_DELETE: Delete WhatsApp template "{{name}}"? For Meta this removes every language variant under that name.
TEMPLATES.CONFIRM_RESYNC: Resync WhatsApp template "{{name}}"? Meta restarts review; Infobip deletes and recreates.

GA4.TITLE: Google Analytics 4
GA4.INTRO: Connect a GA4 property to collect post views on your live site and read them back into Blog Analytics. The service-account key is stored securely on the server and never exposed to the browser.
GA4.MEASUREMENT_HINT: Looks like G-XXXXXXX. This is the gtag.js tag we inject on your live site to start collecting views.
GA4.PROPERTY_HINT: The numeric GA4 property id (e.g. 123456789). Used server-side by the Data API to read your stats back.
GA4.SERVICE_KEY_HINT: Paste the full JSON key of a Google Cloud service account that has access to this GA4 property.
GA4.STEP_1: In Google Analytics, create or open a GA4 property for your website.
GA4.STEP_2: Admin → Data streams → your web stream → copy the Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXX) and paste it below.
GA4.STEP_3: Admin → Property settings → copy the numeric Property ID and paste it below.
GA4.STEP_4: In Google Cloud, create a service account, enable the “Google Analytics Data API”, then create and download a JSON key.
GA4.STEP_5: Admin → Property access management → add the service-account email as a Viewer.
GA4.STEP_6: Paste the JSON key below, enable the plugin, and save.

GSC.TITLE: Google Search Console
GSC.INTRO: Connect a verified Search Console property to pull search impressions, clicks and top queries into Blog Analytics. The service-account key is stored securely on the server.
GSC.SITE_URL_HINT: Only needed if this store uses a custom domain — your slug subdomain works automatically. Use a URL-prefix property (https://example.com/) or a domain property (sc-domain:example.com), exactly as it appears in Search Console.
GSC.SERVICE_KEY_HINT: Paste the full JSON key of a Google Cloud service account that has access to this property.
GSC.HOWTO_TITLE: How to link Google Search Console
GSC.STEP_1: Only for a custom domain: in Google Search Console, add your site and verify ownership (URL-prefix or Domain property).
GSC.STEP_2: Copy the exact property URL and paste it below.
GSC.STEP_3: In Google Cloud, create a service account, enable the “Google Search Console API”, then create and download a JSON key.
GSC.STEP_4: In Search Console → Settings → Users and permissions → add the service-account email (Full or Restricted).
GSC.STEP_5: Paste the JSON key below, enable the plugin, and save.
GSC.ERR_SITE_URL: Enter a valid property URL (https://… or sc-domain:…) or leave empty.

GTAG.TITLE: Google Tag
GTAG.INTRO: Add your Google Tag, Tag Manager container, GA4 or Google Ads tag to your live storefront. We inject the snippet on every page so your tags and marketing pixels fire automatically.
GTAG.TAG_HINT: Accepts GTM-XXXXXXX (Tag Manager), GT-XXXXXXX (Google tag), G-XXXXXXX (GA4) or AW-XXXXXXXXX (Google Ads).
GTAG.STEP_1: Open Google Tag Manager (or your Google tag / Ads account) and create or select a container.
GTAG.STEP_2: Copy the ID — it looks like GTM-XXXXXXX, GT-XXXXXXX, G-XXXXXXX or AW-XXXXXXXXX.
GTAG.STEP_3: Paste it below, enable the plugin, and save. We handle the on-page snippet for you.
GTAG.ERR_TAG: Enter a valid tag / container ID (GTM-…, GT-…, G-… or AW-…).

FBPIXEL.TITLE: Facebook Pixel
FBPIXEL.INTRO: Add your Meta (Facebook) Pixel to your live storefront to measure ad performance and build audiences. We inject the pixel on every page. An optional Conversions API token lets us send server-side events too.
FBPIXEL.PIXEL_HINT: The numeric Meta Pixel ID from Events Manager (usually 15–16 digits).
FBPIXEL.ACCESS_TOKEN_HINT: Optional. Enables server-side events (better attribution). Stored securely and never shown again.
FBPIXEL.STEP_1: In Meta Events Manager, create or open a Pixel (data source).
FBPIXEL.STEP_2: Copy the numeric Pixel ID and paste it below.
FBPIXEL.STEP_3: Optional: under Settings → Conversions API, generate an access token and paste it below. Then enable and save.
FBPIXEL.ERR_PIXEL: Enter a valid numeric Pixel ID.

MKTGUIDE.TITLE: Marketing Tools — setup guide
MKTGUIDE.INTRO: Add Google Tag (Tag Manager) and the Facebook (Meta) Pixel to your live storefront to power marketing tags, retargeting and conversion tracking. Follow the steps for each tool below.
MKTGUIDE.WHAT_TITLE: First — what does each tool do?
MKTGUIDE.WHAT_GTAG_USE: A single container that deploys many tags (GA4, Google Ads, remarketing, custom events) without editing your store's code.
MKTGUIDE.WHAT_FBPIXEL_USE: Measures ad performance, builds retargeting audiences and tracks conversions for Facebook/Instagram ads.
MKTGUIDE.GTAG_LEAD: One container ID covers your store on any address (our subdomain or a custom domain). We inject the snippet on every page for you.
MKTGUIDE.GTAG_S1: Open Google Tag Manager and create an account + a Web container for your store (or reuse an existing one).
MKTGUIDE.GTAG_S2: Copy the container ID from the top of the workspace — it looks like GTM-XXXXXXX. (A Google tag / Ads ID like GT-, G- or AW- also works.)
MKTGUIDE.GTAG_S3: Paste the ID into the Google Tag plugin below, enable it, and save.
MKTGUIDE.GTAG_S4: In Tag Manager, add and publish your tags (GA4, Ads, etc.) — they'll fire on your live store automatically.
MKTGUIDE.FBPIXEL_LEAD: Add your Meta Pixel to measure ads and build audiences. Works on any store address.
MKTGUIDE.FBPIXEL_S1: Open Meta Events Manager and create a data source → Web → Pixel (or open an existing pixel).
MKTGUIDE.FBPIXEL_S2: Copy the numeric Pixel ID (usually 15–16 digits) shown next to the pixel name.
MKTGUIDE.FBPIXEL_S3: Paste it into the Facebook Pixel plugin below, enable it, and save.
MKTGUIDE.FBPIXEL_S4: Use Meta's Pixel Helper browser extension on your live store to confirm it's firing.
MKTGUIDE.FBCAPI_BODY: In Events Manager → Settings → Conversions API, generate an access token and paste it into the plugin's optional token field. This lets us send purchase and lead events server-side, improving accuracy when browsers block the pixel.
MKTGUIDE.NOTE_INJECT: Once enabled, we inject each tag/pixel on every page of your live storefront — no code changes needed.
MKTGUIDE.NOTE_VERIFY: Use Google Tag Assistant or Meta Pixel Helper to verify your tags fire correctly after saving.
MKTGUIDE.NOTE_ISOLATION: Each store uses its own IDs — your tracking is never mixed with other stores.
MKTGUIDE.NOTE_CONSENT: Make sure your storefront's cookie/consent notice covers these marketing tools where required by law.
MKTGUIDE.LINK_GTM_SETUP: Set up a Tag Manager container

GUIDE.TITLE: Google Analytics & Search Console — setup guide
GUIDE.INTRO: Connect Google Analytics 4 (visitors, traffic, sales) and Search Console (how you appear in Google search). Follow the steps for your store's address.
GUIDE.WHICH_TITLE: First — which address is your store on?
GUIDE.CASE_SUB_DO: GA4: full setup below. Search Console: nothing — it's automatic.
GUIDE.CASE_CUSTOM_DO: GA4: full setup below. Search Console: full setup below.
GUIDE.GA4_LEAD: Same whether you're on our subdomain or a custom domain — one property covers your store on any address.
GUIDE.GA4_S1: In Google Analytics, create a property and add a Web data stream for your store URL.
GUIDE.GA4_S2: Copy the Measurement ID (looks like G-XXXXXXX) from the data stream.
GUIDE.GA4_S3: In Admin → Property settings, copy the numeric Property ID (e.g. 123456789).
GUIDE.GA4_S4: In Google Cloud, enable the “Google Analytics Data API”, create a service account, and download a JSON key.
GUIDE.GA4_S5: In Analytics → Admin → Property access management, add the service account email (client_email from the JSON) as Viewer. Uncheck “Notify by email”.
GUIDE.GA4_S6: In your store → Settings → Plugins → Google Analytics 4: paste the Measurement ID, Property ID and JSON key → Test connection → Enable → Save.
GUIDE.GA4_CROSSDOMAIN: Custom-domain tip: if visitors move between your custom domain and the …invopos.shop address in one visit, list both domains in your GA4 data stream → Configure tag settings → Configure your domains.
GUIDE.GSC_A_TITLE: Using our subdomain (yourstore.invopos.shop)? Nothing to do.
GUIDE.GSC_A_BODY: Your search performance is collected automatically and shown under Analytics → Google search. You can leave the Search Console plugin's property field empty.
GUIDE.GSC_B1: Add and verify your domain in Google Search Console (Domain or URL-prefix property, usually a DNS TXT record).
GUIDE.GSC_B2: In Google Cloud, enable the “Google Search Console API”. You can reuse the same service account + JSON key from Part 1.
GUIDE.GSC_B3: In Search Console → Settings → Users and permissions, add the service account email (Full or Restricted).
GUIDE.GSC_B4: In your store → Settings → Plugins → Google Search Console: enter your property (https://yourstore.com/ or sc-domain:yourstore.com) and the JSON key → Test connection → Enable → Save.
GUIDE.OPEN_GSC: Open the Google Search Console plugin
GUIDE.LINK_GA4_USERS: Add users to a GA4 property
GUIDE.NOTE_TIME: First numbers take time — realtime shows within minutes once visitors arrive; full daily reports settle in a few hours, and some metrics take 24–48h.
GUIDE.NOTE_KEY: Keep your JSON key private. It's stored encrypted and never shown again — paste a new one only to replace it.
GUIDE.NOTE_ISOLATION: Each store uses its own GA4 property — your data is never mixed with other stores.
GUIDE.NOTE_WHERE: See your data under Analytics in the main sidebar (blog-only stats live under Blog → Analytics).

AI.TITLE: Content AI
AI.INTRO: Connect an AI provider to generate and improve content across the portal. Keys are stored securely on the server and never exposed to the browser.
AI.CUSTOM_REQUIRED: Base URL and model are required for a custom provider.
AI.TEST_HINT: Runs a quick test generation using the saved configuration. Save changes first.
AI.GET_KEY: How to get an API key
AI.CUSTOM_HELP: Enter the OpenAI-compatible base URL and a model id from your provider.
AI.EMPLOYEE_INTRO: Your key overrides the company-wide Content AI plugin.
AI.DISABLED_TOOLTIP: Content AI is not configured. Open Settings → Plugins → Content AI.
AI.ERR_NOT_CONFIGURED: Content AI is not configured yet. Ask an admin to set it up in Plugins → Content AI.
AI.ERR_UNAVAILABLE: The AI service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.
AI.ERR_AUTH_FAILED: The stored AI key was rejected. An admin must update it in Plugins → Content AI.
AI.ERR_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE: The AI provider account is out of credits.
AI.ERR_RATE_LIMITED: Too many requests — please wait a moment and try again.
AI.ERR_BAD_REQUEST: The AI provider rejected the request. Please try again.
AI.ERR_TOO_LONG: The selection is too long (max 8000 characters).
AI.ERR_TIMEOUT: The request timed out. Please try again.
